newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares jump as foreign demand buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares jump as foreign demand buoyant.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 3.52 percent on Friday, pushed up by continued foreign buying to end the week 45 points higher, and market participants said the market was poised for more gains as demand remained buoyant.

"Investors, especially foreign ones, seem to be buying without limits, while most individual share-owners of newly privatised companies are not willing to sell," said Nina Jarc, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
She said investors showed most interest in drug company Lek, food firm Kolinska, bank SKB, health resort operator Terme Catez and food maker Droga.
The SBI index rose 44.92 points to 1,322.8. Overall 13 shares rose, three fell, one was unchanged and eight were untraded. Turnover rose to 550.4 million tolars from 224.6 million.
Issue A of drug company Lek was most actively traded, soaring 8.8 percent to 27,200 tolars on volume of 9,776 shares for total turnover of 256.5 million tolars.
"Lek was pushed up mainly by foreign investors who believe its price is low compared to the price of similar firms elsewhere," one broker said.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, rising 9.63 percent to 20,830 on volume of 31 shares for total turnover of 0.6 million tolars.
Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska Banka were the leading decliners, falling 5.97 percent to 11,650 on volume of 40 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars.
